title: CAP, PACELC and the guarantee you give up on purpose

videos.script: Every database in this course keeps more than one copy of your data. {{copies}} That is where all three get their speed and their survival. It is also where they get a choice the relational database on one machine never had to make. {{choice}} Picture two copies of a shop, one in São Paulo and one in Lisbon. The cable between them fails. A customer on each side buys the last monitor. {{partition}} Each copy can refuse the sale, or make it without knowing about the other. There is no third move. That is the CAP theorem, stated the way its proof states it. {{cap}} Then the cable is fixed, and a quieter cost appears. Keeping both copies in step means waiting for the far one, on every write. {{pacelc}} So the question is never which database is consistent. It is which operation needs consistency, and which would rather be fast. {{table}} After that you build the lab. A virtual machine, Docker, and three servers: MongoDB, Redis and Cassandra. {{lab}} You will start all three, talk to each one, and see what each costs in memory. And you will meet, on purpose, the errors you are most likely to meet by accident. {{errors}}
